ticks.by: Narrow Highway - the Riemann hypothesis proved, restated for precision, 2026-11-
ticks.claim: Every non-trivial zero of the Riemann zeta function has real part 1/2: PROVED - a machine-checked Lean proof (L. Alpöge, released 2026-11-20); no human-readable proof yet. On 2026-11-21 the Lean FRO and the Mathlib Initiative certified both the statement and the proof. The statement is Mathlib's own RiemannHypothesis (read here at the pinned revision on 2026-11-20); #print axioms on the headline theorems gives only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound; and the proof is accepted by Lean's kernel and by independent checkers - nanoda, lean4lean, and con-leche and con-ron, which carry a formal proof that they cannot accept a false proof. With an independent formalization of Robin (1984) it yields Robin's inequality for every n > 5040 and Lagarias's for every n >= 1, statements with no zeta function in them. NOT YET: a proof mathematicians can read; the Clay prize, whose rules ask for publication and two years. The generalized hypothesis is proved for Dirichlet L-functions only. The engine has not re-run the proof (the kernel checks need 83-99 GiB of memory and up to 72 hours); this mark cites the certification and seals nothing. The bounds on this stick stay as they were: zeros counted and checked here, now instances of a theorem.
ticks.source: L. Alpöge, Lean proof of the Riemann hypothesis and GRH for Dirichlet L-functions (released 2026-11-20, alpo.ge); Lean FRO and Mathlib Initiative, joint statement (2026-11-21); A. Sutherland, verification record, math.mit.edu/~drew/grh (2026-11-24)

Both were true when minted. Since 2026-11-20 the Riemann hypothesis is proved - a machine-checked Lean proof (Alpöge; statement and proof certified by the Lean FRO and the Mathlib Initiative, 2026-11-21); no human-readable proof yet - see this stick's closed mark. The rest of both notes stands: Deligne's 1974 theorem is the Riemann hypothesis over FINITE FIELDS, a different theorem; a lower bound on the proportion of zeros on the critical line is not the hypothesis; and the 67.2% bound itself is still a claim the engine has not re-derived.

stick_the_symmetry.question: The symmetry
references: the functional equation's reflection s <-> 1-s, fixed line Re = 1/2
self-adjoint -> real line; Cayley -> unit circle; Frobenius -> |alpha| = sqrt(q)
stick_the_symmetry.statement: Across the Riemann arc one structure recurs: the zeros sit on the fixed set of a symmetry. The functional equation reflects s to 1-s about Re = 1/2; a self-adjoint operator reflects its spectrum onto the real line; the Cayley map carries that line to the unit circle; Frobenius pins |alpha| = sqrt(q). RH is the statement that the zeros are as symmetric as the law allows.
